title: The Trophy and the Table

not_found: A public, citable estimate of the one-season cost of replacing a manager for a single club. Handled by redesign (coordinator, 2026-10-04): the case poses it as a student-chosen range and a break-even rather than a fixed number. (The forecast slope, formerly also not found, is DERIVED from ten Wikipedia season tables.)
Official premierleague.com final-table page in machine-readable form (JavaScript-rendered). Table cited to Wikipedia (S1, MEDIUM) and cross-checked row by row against the bundle CSV.
excluded_sources: Football-Data.co.uk CSV files: link-only, never bundled or fetched by the case (terms S5).
FBref expected-goals data: discontinued (Opta, 20 Jan 2026); never cited.
StatsBomb open data / Understat: optional extension only; no figure from either is used.
Injury counts from fan or hobby sites: not used as fact. The citable record is the Premier League report (S4).
Al Jazeera's report gave the Europa League final as 25 May 2025; Wikipedia gives 21 May 2025 (a Wednesday); the 21 May date is used and the Al Jazeera date rejected.
ESPN standings page: the fetch summary garbled the bottom-three rows, so ESPN was not used as a cross-check.
scenario_constructions: The decision point (a board meeting in the last days of May 2025) is constructed. The club's real decision and statement are public but are withheld from the student document and surfaced in the guide's Close. The unnamed board member and the boardroom scene are invented; no real person is quoted or given invented dialogue.

MA2 (reset cost) is not fixed by the case: students choose a range; 2 points is only the balance-test evaluation point. MA3 (same goal difference next season) and the scoring convention MA3b are scenario assumptions with no citation. MA1 is derived (Appendix E).

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Forecast slope: a club that missed its season's line by r points misses by about slope x r points the next season (DERIVED from ten seasons of Wikipedia tables, not invented)
modeling_assumptions.value: 0.11 (pooled 0.109; 95% range about -0.05 to 0.27, read as 0 to 0.27)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Regression of next-season residual on this-season residual, 153 club-pairs across nine season pairs (2015/16 to 2024/25); points from results so 2023/24 deductions are excluded. Sampling caveat: seasons of 20 clubs are small; per-pair slopes -0.15 to 0.38; typical clubs mostly missed by under 8 points; a forecast, not a causal claim.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: One-season reset cost, in points, of replacing the manager: NOT fixed by the case; students choose and defend a range (the case suggests 0 to 4)
modeling_assumptions.value: student's choice; balance-test evaluation point 2 points (midpoint of the suggested 0-4 range)
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public source. The earlier drafts fixed 6 then 2 points; that was rejected as tuning. The case now poses the break-even (a x |shortfall| = 1.58 points at slope 0.11) and asks whether a reset cost below it is plausible. The 2-point test point exists only so the SPEC balance margin can be computed; it is not a case claim.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Load-bearing; the break-even is the real question.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: The club's goal difference next season is the same under both options
modeling_assumptions.basis: Isolates the two choices; leaves out transfers, injuries and the Champions League schedule.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Scoring convention: both options start from the model's predicted points; Keep = predicted - slope x |shortfall|; Change = predicted - the student's chosen reset cost; percent margin divides by the smaller value
modeling_assumptions.basis: Added after the cold-solve and twist probes found students could start from actual points or pick different margin denominators.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Residuals are described in residual spreads, treating the other clubs' misses as ordinary bell-shaped variation
modeling_assumptions.basis: With 20 clubs the shape cannot be checked; D5 asks the student to say what that costs.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Affects how extreme the club's miss sounds, not the points arithmetic in D4.

sensitivity_note: SPEC Section 6 applies lightly: the case concerns a living, named manager and a real club's real decision. The facilitator note (required) tells the guide that students are judging a model, not a person; the case uses public record only, speculates on no one's motives, quotes no one, and withholds the real decision until the Close.

balance.argument_a: Keep the Winner is the better bet if the reset cost exceeds the break-even of 0.11 x 14.40 = 1.58 points. Ten seasons of tables say a club's miss forecasts only about 0.11 of itself next season, and the 14 club-seasons that missed by 5 or more points averaged +1.15 the next year. A new manager has a real reset cost, the Premier League itself documented all four senior centre-backs injured at once, and one season of 20 clubs cannot separate luck or injuries from management. At the 2-point test point Keep leads 50.82 to 50.40.
balance.argument_b: Change After 17th is the better bet if the reset cost is below the break-even, which is 1.58 points at slope 0.11 and 3.89 at the top of the range (0.27). The club sits 4.32 residual spreads below its line, and no club in ten seasons missed its line by as much (largest earlier miss: Manchester City 2019/20, about 11.2), so a slope fitted on typical clubs may understate it. At slope 0.27 Replace wins for reset costs below 3.89 points, about 97% of the suggested 0 to 4 range, and at the 2-point test point leads 50.40 to 48.52 (3.89%). The model cannot show a manager caused any of it, but cannot rule it out either.
balance.margin_basis: Primary metric is expected 2025/26 points. E_A = L - slope x |shortfall| (L and shortfall from the D3 line); E_B = L - reset cost. The reset cost is not fixed by the case, so the SPEC margin is computed at a stated TEST POINT of 2 points (midpoint of the suggested 0-4 range): margin = (higher - lower) / lower. The substantive question is the break-even reset cost a x |shortfall|.
balance.twist_effect: Facilitator adds: no club in the ten Appendix E seasons ever missed its own season's line by as much as this club, and the slope was fitted on typical clubs; suppose that for a miss this size the slope is the top of the range, 0.27. The forecast next-season shortfall rises from 1.58 to 3.89 points, so the break-even reset cost rises to 3.89. At the 2-point test point E_A falls from 50.82 to 48.52 against E_B = 50.40: the winner flips from Keep the Winner (0.82%) to Change After 17th (3.89%). Option B is unaffected (it pays only the reset cost, per MA3b); a student who charges B the slope-based shortfall as well would make the twist do nothing, and the guide states aloud that B pays only its reset cost. A what-if on an already-disclosed range, never a measured fact. It does not make Replace obviously right: a reset cost above 3.89 still favours Keep.
balance.stability: At the 2-point test point the margin is 0.82%. At +/-50% flex, slope +50% (0.165) flips the winner to Change (0.75%); reset cost -50% (1 point) flips the winner to Change (1.15%); slope -50% and reset cost +50% widen Keep's lead to 2.40% and 2.87%. No flex breaches the 20% cap. The verdict is fragile and the case says so; the break-even framing makes that explicit.
balance.verdict_under_range: Over the suggested 0-4 range of reset costs, Replace wins for costs below 1.58 (about 40% of the range) and Keep for costs above it (about 60%), at slope 0.11; at slope 0.27 Replace wins below 3.89 (about 97%). Two-sided at the central slope; the case says so.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: The forecast slope is derived from ten seasons of small 20-club tables with a 95% range of about -0.05 to 0.27; the true forecast for this one club next season is an irreducible unknown. +50% (0.165) flips the winner to Change at the test point (0.75%, inside the cap); -50% (0.055) widens Keep's lead to 2.40%.

The reset cost has no citable estimate for one club; students choose a range and the 2-point test point is only a midpoint for the balance check. -50% (1 point) flips the winner to Change (1.15%, inside the cap); +50% (3 points) widens Keep's lead to 2.87%.

deliverables.text: A scatter plot of the 20 clubs with a line of best fit and its equation; correlation described; slope interpreted in points per goal; mean goal difference and mean points found and compared with where the line passes.

A residual table for all 20 clubs: predicted points, residual, the club's residual, next-largest shortfall, largest surplus, residuals averaging about zero, residual spread described with Variability, and how many spreads below the line the club sits.

An outlier check: the line refitted on the other 19 clubs, the club's residual against it, the other 19 clubs' residual spread, spreads below the line, and a statement on whether the shortfall is an artifact of the club pulling the line.

A break-even comparison: forecast next-season shortfall under Keep (slope 0.11 x shortfall), expected points, the break-even reset cost, the student's own defended reset-cost range, and the winner and percent margin at the low, middle and high ends of that range.

GRADED: what the model leaves out -- at least four limits each tied to a number or fact, using Sample Size and Random, each marked as pushing toward A or B, the single most decision-changing limit, and the free data (Appendix C) that would test it.

context_glossary.desc: A European club soccer tournament that sits one step below the Champions League. Clubs from many countries qualify by how they finish in their home leagues, and the winner earns a place in the next Champions League.
The top European club soccer tournament, contested by leading clubs from many countries and one of the competitions clubs most want to qualify for.
In British football, the head coach: the person with overall responsibility for running the team, including picking the squad and setting tactics.
A central defender, whose main job is to defend the area in front of the goal and stop the other team from scoring.
Sent down to a lower division. In the Premier League the bottom three of 20 clubs drop to the second division at the end of a season.
Goals a club scored in league games minus goals it conceded. A club that scores 64 and concedes 65 has a goal difference of minus 1.

catalog.ask: A club won a trophy and finished 17th in its league. A line through the whole league table says it missed its points by a mile, but ten past seasons say a miss like that forecasts only a small miss next year. Replacing the manager only pays off if the cost of a reset is smaller than that. Is it?
